completeness.reason: REQ_POWER_DERATING and REQ_THERMAL_ACTUATOR_FAILSAFE (jointly with ARCH_COOLANT_ACTUATOR_IF) are fully covered. For REQ_SUSTAINED_DISCHARGE_LIMIT the body says that a sustained-load limit exists and where its input comes from, but none of the externally visible terms of the requirement is stated: the 250 A cap, the trailing 10 s average, the window from the average reaching 250 A until it falls below again, and that full power stays available below that average for a short peak. It is covered at outline level only, so the detail rests on the swreq alone.
completeness.suggestion: Add one clause restating those obligations in design terms: the sustained-load share is 100 % while the trailing 10 s average pack discharge current is below 250 A, and holds the current at 250 A from the moment that average reaches 250 A until it falls below it again.

consistency.reason: The only sibling sharing a parent is ARCH_COOLANT_ACTUATOR_IF (REQ_THERMAL_ACTUATOR_FAILSAFE) and the split is clean: it owns the 2 s acknowledgement timer and the unconfirmed verdict and "never decides a power limit itself", while this element turns that verdict into the flat 30 % and owns the published power. REQ_POWER_DERATING and REQ_SUSTAINED_DISCHARGE_LIMIT are satisfied by this element alone, and its 250 A / 10 s limit sits below, without contradicting, the 350 A / 100 ms trip owned by ARCH_CURRENT_PATH_MONITOR.

design_clarity.reason: The ramp, the flat 30 %, the minimum-of-three rule with its rationale and the reuse of the existing current acquisition are concrete choices, but the sustained-load limit is only "a sustained-load limit from the pack discharge current": the body names no 10 s trailing average, no 250 A threshold, no engage/release rule and no way a current limit becomes a power share. The fixed 250 A / 320 A = 78.125 % share exists only in SWREQ_SUSTAINED_LOAD_LIMIT and the code, and the sentence equally fits proportional scaling to the measured average (250 A / average), which the earlier revision of that swreq used, so the element does not say which design was chosen.
design_clarity.suggestion: Name the sustained-load choice the way the other two limits are named: a trailing 10 s average of the pack discharge current, engaged at or above 250 A and released below it, 100 % share otherwise, and the fixed 250 A / 320 A full-power-current share (78.125 %) applied while engaged, with the stated assumption that full permitted power draws 320 A (or state proportional scaling if that is the intent).

implementability.reason: One component with three inputs and one published output is a single bounded implementation, but the cross-stream boundary is loose: this element takes the pack current from ARCH_CURRENT_PATH_MONITOR, yet that element, its only swreq (SWREQ_OVERCURRENT_DEBOUNCE) and the cell-protection diagram offer only a debounced overcurrent condition and a "filtered pack current" to the supervisor, not a current signal for a second consumer, and the dependency is prose plus an unlinked diagram box rather than an explicit relation. The body also does not say which element forms the 10 s average, so an implementer must decide the signal used (1 ms samples or the filtered value), its timestamping and where the averaging lives.
implementability.suggestion: State that the calculator consumes the discharge-positive current samples of the monitor (or whichever signal is intended) and owns the 10 s averaging, and close the monitor side: list the calculator as a consumer in the cell-protection diagram or element text, or give the dependency an explicit link, so both streams promise the same signal.

parent_fit.reason: Each of the three parents is engaged by its own design content: the 100 % at 55 °C to 0 % at 60 °C ramp for REQ_POWER_DERATING, the flat 30 % on an unconfirmed verdict for REQ_THERMAL_ACTUATOR_FAILSAFE (the 2 s timer and the verdict belong to the sibling ARCH_COOLANT_ACTUATOR_IF), and a third limit derived from the pack discharge current and merged by minimum for REQ_SUSTAINED_DISCHARGE_LIMIT. This is substantive, not a nominal link; the thin detail of the sustained-load part is scored under design_clarity and completeness rather than counted twice here.

summary: The element cleanly designs the 55-60 °C ramp, the flat 30 % fallback and the minimum-of-three publication and is consistent with its only sibling, but the sustained-load limit is named only in outline (no 10 s trailing average, no 250 A engage/release rule, no current-to-power-share conversion) and its dependency on the Pack Current Path Monitor is asserted only from this side, so design clarity, completeness and implementability each lose a point.
